stationary-person field and motion-based uniform reduction

main_argument_chains.claim: A spatial BWOP model identifies local temperature structure and supplies evidence for later reductions.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the high-fidelity field to locate hot/cold regions and bound when a lumped temperature can be trusted.
support_steps: Declare fluid and boundary assumptions.
Derive water-air and hot-water-tube coefficients.
State the three-dimensional conservation system.
Restore the real faucet and overflow in FLUENT.
Interpret isotherms with volume-integral statistics.

main_argument_chains.claim: Occupied-bath behavior allows the paper to move from spatial CFD to a lumped loss model and compare two controls.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat the control results as conditional on the instant-mixing and time-scale assumptions.
support_steps: Show stationary-person and body-surface nonuniformity.
Invoke agitation as a mixing response.
Sum water-air and tub-wall losses into Qd.
Insert Qd into CI and DCI recurrences.
Report each schedule's resource, comfort, and operation measures.

main_argument_chains.claim: The paper selects DCI by combining four criteria and then translates the choice into user action.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Preserve the raw-to-decision trace, but require criterion-direction and normalization audit before reusing the ranking.
support_steps: Assemble the CI/DCI raw criteria.
Define an ideal allocation.
Normalize into an FCE matrix.
Apply weights and compare scalar distances.
Offer continuous and threshold user branches with safety notes.

main_argument_chains.claim: Scenario and bubble extensions reuse the baseline outputs to identify transfer boundaries.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Recalibrate coupled geometry and material properties rather than carrying nominal trends to a new tub.
support_steps: Vary inflow velocity, inflow temperature, and air temperature.
Compare area, volume, material, and occupant-volume curves.
Rank water volume as the dominant BWP factor.
Replace direct surface loss with bubble-layer conduction.
Compare effective-conductivity cooling curves.
